title: Protected budget reservations
description: Objective: add atomic executor admission reservations on the conserved ledger from task-a5def097bcb7495e935204bd845160b4. Deliverable: packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.ts, its one-line .js bridge, and focused tests for reserve-or-refuse, one-use activation, and proven-never-started cancellation across caller-supplied EXECUTION, VERIFICATION, INDEPENDENT_REVIEW, FINAL_ACCEPTANCE, and CONTINGENCY amounts. NOT in scope: choosing reserve amounts, policy evaluation or approval validation, provider quotes, measurements, settlement/quarantine, fan-out materialization/integration, persistence, or package-root export. Hard dependencies: task-7dc2e4870d7d4096a1be7b5991e50e94 and task-a5def097bcb7495e935204bd845160b4 must be DONE unchanged. Owned paths: budget-reservation.ts, budget-reservation.js, budget-reservation.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler exec vitest run --root ../.. packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: Admission atomically reserves the complete caller-supplied execution, verification, independent-review, final-acceptance, and contingency set or returns a frozen refusal with no state or ledger-entry change.
The exact available boundary succeeds, one unit short refuses, and no operation can spend or reclassify a protected purpose through an EXECUTION reservation.

A reservation activates at most once; stale-version activate/cancel competitors yield one legal winner and a zero-effect loser, while cancellation refunds only a proven-never-started refundable reservation.

Malformed/duplicate purpose entries, zero or unsafe quantities, missing protected purposes, closed/overdrawn accounts, and policy outcomes other than an already-validated allowance or current human approval fail closed in deterministic precedence.
Both TypeScript files are <=250 physical lines, the bridge is one exact re-export line, and the focused verification command exits 0.
taskRails: Reserve minima are caller-supplied immutable facts; do not guess token, currency, verification, review, acceptance, or contingency amounts.
Consume only a narrow already-validated policy/approval gate structurally aligned with the committed core interface; do not forge approvals, duplicate evaluatePolicy, or import @moe/core.
Production and test TypeScript files must each be <=250 physical lines; stage only the three explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — packages/scheduler/src/budget/budget-reservation.test.ts (<=250 physical HARD; assert-the-reason-code rail: every refusal asserts its exact code AND which layer refused; mutation red-checks named). Cases: (1) ALL-OR-NONE ADMISSION: reserveForAdmission over a caller-supplied five-purpose amount set against a ledger-derived available view — success returns a frozen ReservationRecord (per-purpose lines, deterministic reservationId from accountId+admissionRef, state RESERVED, version) + the updated frozen bucket view; ANY shortfall returns a frozen refusal with ZERO state/ledger change (deep-equal before/after — the no-partial-set rule, design 12.2/587); (2) EXACT BOUNDARY: reserving exactly the available amount succeeds; one unit more refuses (per meter, per purpose — both boundary directions asserted); (3) PURPOSE PROTECTION: no operation path can spend or reclassify a protected-purpose line through the EXECUTION line — attempt activation/cancel calls that reference a protected line via the execution entry -> refusal with exact code; protected lines remain untouched after EXECUTION activation (deep-equal on the protected entries); (4) ONE-USE ACTIVATION: activateReservation succeeds at most once (RESERVED->ACTIVATED with version bump); a second activate and a concurrent stale-expectedVersion activate/cancel competitor pair yield ONE legal winner and a ZERO-EFFECT loser (exact stale code; the exactly-one-successor discipline); (5) CANCELLATION: refunds ONLY a proven-never-started refundable reservation (neverStartedProof ref required; activated -> refuse; missing proof -> refuse; refund restores the bucket view deep-equal to pre-reserve); (6) FAIL-CLOSED PRECEDENCE (deterministic order asserted): malformed input (contract layer) > duplicate purpose entries > zero/unsafe quantities > missing protected purposes (all four protected lines REQUIRED — absent -> refuse; caller-supplied amounts are facts, zero-amount protected line is a refusal not a default) > closed/overdrawn account state > gate rejection (policy outcome other than validated ALLOW / current human approval — wrong outcome string, stale validity, absent gate each with distinct codes); (7) hostile inputs via '../runtime-shape.js'. RED confirmed by the task's focused command: "Error: Cannot find module './budget-reservation.js'", Test Files 1 failed, Tests: no tests — failing because the production surface is absent, not because of a typo. Covers all seven planned families: (1) all-or-none — a one-unit shortfall on a single MS line refuses with zero state change (result.view `toBe` the input reference AND a JSON snapshot deep-equal) and the failure arm's reservation is null, so no partial set can be minted; (2) exact boundary — reserving exactly 90/1 drives both meters to available 0, and 89 MS or 0 AT each refuse (both directions, both meters); (3) purpose protection — a protected line relabelled EXECUTION refuses PROTECTED_PURPOSE_MISSING, an EXECUTION line relabelled onto a protected purpose refuses DUPLICATE_PURPOSE, and after activation the protected lines deep-equal their pre-activation selves; (4) one-use activation — RESERVED->ACTIVATED with a version bump and the view returned by REFERENCE (activation moves no units), a second activate at the fresh version refuses ALREADY_SETTLED, and a stale-expectedVersion activate/cancel competitor PAIR each refuse STALE_VERSION with a byte-identical view; (5) cancellation — refund restores the meters deep-equal to the pre-reserve snapshot; activated, no-proof, over-refund and unknown-meter refunds each refuse with their own code; (6) fail-closed precedence — a 15-row table where EVERY row supplies NO gate at all, so each row proves its own code beats the gate check rather than merely reaching some refusal, plus a 7-row gate-layer table; (7) hostile inputs — forged gate with an extra key, gate reached through the prototype chain, and a gate allowance behind an accessor all refuse GATE_MALFORMED. Guarding the case list per pattern-guard-the-case-list-not-just-the-cases: every refusal funnels through one `codes()` helper that records the code into an `observed` set, and the final test asserts observed EQUALS BUDGET_RESERVATION_ISSUE_CODES exactly, so a published code with no case fails the suite and no code is excluded as unreachable. Vocabulary is asserted against the production surface (deriveReservationId is exported and tested for a length-prefixed non-colliding identity, and the ADMISSION_PURPOSE_RESERVE_CONTRACT mapping is checked to land inside the landed BUDGET_RESERVE_PURPOSES), not against a test-local reimplementation.

implementationPlan.note: GREEN. budget-reservation.ts 249 lines, budget-reservation.js is the exact one-line re-export, budget-reservation.test.ts 250 lines. `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler typecheck` exit 0; focused vitest 40/40 passed. Pure functions over caller-supplied state, no registries, no Date/random: reserveForAdmission(view, admission, gate), activateReservation(view, reservation, {expectedVersion, attemptRef}), cancelReservation(view, reservation, {expectedVersion, neverStartedProofRef}), deriveReservationId(accountId, admissionRef). Imports only ../runtime-shape.js, ./budget-account.js (MAX_BUDGET_VERSION) and ./budget-contract.js — no @moe/core, no @moe/contracts. THREE PLAN DEVIATIONS, each forced and each an improvement: (1) cancelReservation takes the VIEW as its first argument, which the plan's signature omitted — a pure function cannot restore the bucket view on refund without it, and the DoD explicitly requires the refund to restore the view; activateReservation takes the view too and returns it BY REFERENCE, which turns "activation moves no units" into a `toBe` assertion instead of a deep-equal one. (2) checkTransition's precedence puts STALE_VERSION ahead of ALREADY_SETTLED so the stale competitor reports the stale code as the plan asked, while a second activate at the FRESH version reports ALREADY_SETTLED — both losers are covered with distinct codes. (3) Issue messages are derived from the code (`code.slice("BUDGET_RESERVATION_".length)` humanised) rather than hand-written per site; this was the compaction that fit 18 codes and ~20 guard rows under the hard 249-line cap without dropping a single guard, and it makes prose drift from the code structurally impossible. THE STALE-COMPETITOR SEMANTICS ARE WORTH THE NEXT AGENT'S ATTENTION: with pure functions and no registry, two competitors that both hold the version-0 record would BOTH succeed — one-use is only enforced when the loser is applied to the successor the winner produced. My first test asserted the wrong thing and passed the pre-activation record, so it caught the loser succeeding; the fixed test applies the loser to winner.reservation with its stale expectedVersion 0 and gets STALE_VERSION. That is the compare-and-swap discipline this module supplies the fence for; the persistence layer is what refuses the second write. Two other test expectations were wrong and the production code was right: relabelling VERIFICATION@MS to EXECUTION collides with the existing EXECUTION@MS line so it reports DUPLICATE_PURPOSE, not PROTECTED_PURPOSE_MISSING (the test now drops the original execution line first, isolating the reclassification), and remapping every line onto one absent meter duplicated (EXECUTION, meter:absent) so it reported DUPLICATE_PURPOSE, not UNKNOWN_METER (the test now moves only the uniquely-purposed CONTINGENCY line). Both are instances of pattern-one-fixture-per-predicate-leg: an over-determined fixture was being blocked by the wrong leg.

(5) Laundering red-team: a forged gate with an extra `forced: true` key, a gate reached through the prototype chain, and an allowance behind an accessor all refuse GATE_MALFORMED; a frozen reservation throws TypeError on assignment; a boundary refusal returns the caller's view BY REFERENCE and a JSON snapshot proves it byte-identical. (6) No scratch files; the mutation backup lived outside the repo and is deleted. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW — three limitations I want on the record rather than hidden. (a) AT-MOST-ONE RESERVATION PER ADMISSION IS NOT ENFORCED HERE. With no registry, a caller who passes the already-shifted view with its matching expectedVersion can reserve the same admissionRef twice and mint the same deterministic reservationId twice. That is exactly why the identity is deterministic and length-prefixed: persistence (explicitly out of scope) enforces at-most-one by inserting on reservationId. The same applies to one-use activation — this module supplies the compare-and-swap fence, the store must reject the second write. (b) `fail()` deep-freezes the result, which holds the caller's view by reference, so a refusal freezes the caller's view object. This is the landed sibling's behaviour (budget-account.ts) and is deliberate, but it is a visible side effect on a refusal path. (c) The gate is checked LAST by the plan's pinned precedence, so an unauthorized caller with a shortfall learns INSUFFICIENT_AVAILABLE before being refused for authority. Minor and intentional; flagged because a reviewer will notice. Also noted: an empty amounts array refuses as MALFORMED rather than PROTECTED_PURPOSE_MISSING, since an admission with no lines has no shape to evaluate.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Direct plan (fifth budget/scheduler sibling; conventions locked; governor card written at full fidelity against landed surfaces). Design choices: (1) ADMISSION_PURPOSES as a module-local five-tuple (EXECUTION + four protected) with an explicit mapping comment onto the landed contract RESERVE_PURPOSES (INDEPENDENT_REVIEW->REVIEW, FINAL_ACCEPTANCE->ACCEPTANCE_PROCESSING) — the task text and the landed vocabulary use different spellings; inventing new contract entries or editing budget-contract.ts (unowned) are both wrong, and EXECUTION is the admitted work, not a contract reserve purpose (design 587). (2) Pure caller-supplied-state functions, no registries (sibling precedent — determinism + repeat-call deep-equal). (3) Three-layer issue codes (contract BUDGET_*, account BUDGET_ACCOUNT_*, new BUDGET_RESERVATION_*) so the assert-which-layer rail is satisfiable. (4) Gate as narrow structural mirror of the committed core shapes ({decisionRef, outcome:'ALLOW'} / {approvalRef, decision:'APPROVE', validity:'CURRENT'}) — already-validated facts only, no evaluatePolicy duplication, no @moe/core import (task rail). (5) Activation is a one-use MARKER binding attemptRef — bucket movement to COMMITTED belongs to settlement (17.04/17.05); cancel refunds RESERVED->AVAILABLE only with a never-started proof ref (design 12.2 pre-active tombstone analogue).

planningNotes.risks: (1) Partial-set laundering is THE conservation hazard — all-or-none mutation red-check mandatory. (2) Purpose reclassification through the EXECUTION line would let execution spend consume proof reserves (design 587's exact prohibition) — fence + red-check. (3) Double-activation under version races — exactly-one-winner asserted (aliasing gotcha precedent). (4) Vocabulary spelling drift between the task card and the landed contract — the local mapping comment is the honest resolution; editing unowned files is not. (5) Gate forgery — structural mirror validated hostile; wrong-outcome/stale-validity distinct codes. (6) 250-pressure on the test (seven families): tighten fixtures, never drop assertions. (7) Shared tree: 17.04 WORKING — three-path commit, by-path attribution.
